SUBJECT: Preliminary Volume and Share Estimates - November 1989

INDUSTRY

November sales of 50.7 billion units were 8.6% below last year (-7.6% calendar adjusted). This volume decline was primarily the result of more restrictive allocation terms imposed on the trade by most manufacturers during November of this year versus last year (exhibit A). For example, R.J. Reynolds in an effort to eliminate loading, restricted its accounts to 115% of an average week on major brands and 110% on minor ones this November versus 150%/110% respectively last November. R.J.R. was the only manufacturer to raise prices in November, effective November 27th.

Longer timeframes were also impacted by trade program activity with declines ranging from 5.0% year-to-date to 6.3% for the latest 3 months.

PHILIP MORRIS

November sales of 21.4 billion units declined 4.2% versus last year. During November 1989 accounts were restricted to 120% of an average week on all brands except 140% on Cambridge and Alpine. In contrast, during November 1988 accounts were permitted 125% of an average week on all brands. Moreover, during the week ending November 28th, 1988, accounts in California were allowed an additional 50% over and above their 125% allocation, due to inventory needed as a result of the January 1st 25¢ tax hike.

Share

P.M.'s monthly share of 42.2 was slightly above average due to the varying allocation programs of the other manufacturers. On a year-to-date basis, P.M. realized an increase of 1.6 points versus last year to 41.8 share of market.
